sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Israel Reconsiders Inquiry into Deadliest Security Failure After 64 Killed, 19 Kidnapped
cards.content: Three years after the deadliest Israel security failure, questions persist about who should pay the price for the attacks that killed 64 people and kidnapped 19. The attacks, blamed on Hamas, were the deadliest Israel had suffered since its creation in 1948. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected calls for a state inquiry, instead proposing a national commission of inquiry. Critics argue that Netanyahu's refusal to accept responsibility is part of the reason for the ongoing pain and divisions in Israel.

cards.title: Israel's Deadliest Attack: Family of Victims Demands Accountability
cards.content: Inbar Goldstein, whose brother and niece were killed in the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel's border with Gaza, demands accountability from the government. Three years on, there is still no independent state inquiry into the attack that killed 64 people and kidnapped 251 others. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blames his security chiefs for the failure, but critics question his own role in the security lapse. Netanyahu is running for re-election, despite the attack being the deadliest Israel had suffered since its creation in 1948. Calls for accountability are growing, with campaigners seeking a state commission of inquiry.

cards.title: Sri Lanka's ex-first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa arrested in charity fraud probe
cards.content: Sri Lanka's former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa was arrested over allegations that a charity she is linked to misused donations raised for a children's hospital. The charity, Siriliya Saviya, allegedly collected 10 million rupees ($30,300) for a specialized scanner, but officials claim the scanner had already been donated by the Chinese government. Rajapaksa denied any wrongdoing and stated the money has not been misappropriated. Her husband, former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, is a key figure in the investigation, and his family has faced corruption allegations in the past. The development marks a significant moment in Sri Lanka's efforts to combat corruption.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: IMF Warns of Global Economic Pressure from AI, Soaring Energy Costs, and Debt
cards.content: The International Monetary Fund's head, Kristalina Georgieva, warned that artificial intelligence is adding pressure that threatens global economic growth, urging policymakers to address debt issues. AI is a key driver of countries' fortunes, but the triple forces of AI advancement, soaring energy costs, and record public debt are challenging growth. The IMF estimates AI could add 0.5% to annual world growth, but benefits are likely concentrated, increasing the risk of economic inequality. Inflation worries and ballooning public debt are also concerns, with interest rates set to climb higher.

cards.title: Temasek Warns AI Trade Reversal Poses Biggest Risk to Markets
cards.content: The unwinding of the artificial intelligence trade poses the biggest risk to markets, according to Temasek's chief investment officer, Rohit Sipahimalani. He noted that roughly half the stocks in the Russell 3000 are at least 20% below their June highs, highlighting market resilience dependent on a small group of winners. A reversal in the AI trade could be triggered by safety concerns, tighter regulation, or signs of insufficient returns. Temasek remains bullish on AI, with about half of its exposure currently in publicly traded assets, which can be adjusted as the industry evolves. Sipahimalani warned that AI is a fast-changing environment that requires flexibility to pivot.

cards.title: BitMEX CEO predicts AI boom will lead to crash, bailout, benefiting crypto
cards.content: Former BitMEX CEO Arthur Hayes predicts that the artificial intelligence boom will eventually lead to a crash and a bailout, benefiting crypto. He believes that the massive investment in AI data centers will ultimately result in overcapacity, setting the stage for a downturn. Hayes points to financial history, citing that every major technological rollout is overbuilt, followed by a crash and bailout. He sees bitcoin and other crypto as the asset that will perform best during the bailout, advising investors to be patient. The AI boom is expected to create an abundance of computing power, which Hayes' new project Flop aims to utilize for AI-agent payments.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Russian lab technician dies from pneumonic plague in Siberia
cards.content: A Russian lab technician died at a plague research centre in Siberia, sparking concerns about pneumonic plague spread. The 28-year-old woman, Darya Shipilova, worked at the Anti-Plague Institute in Irkutsk region. Experts say the case is unlikely to lead to a global outbreak due to pneumonic plague's requirement for symptoms before transmission, making it easily contained. Antibiotics are widely available to treat the disease, and public health measures have identified and are monitoring contacts, with none showing symptoms. The World Health Organisation's initial risk assessment is moderate to low for Irkutsk and very low for the Russian Federation as a whole.

cards.title: Study Finds Hang-Xiety Affects 18.3% of Students, Linked to Shyness
cards.content: A hangover is not the only consequence of a night out drinking, as many people experience a phenomenon known as hang-xiety, characterized by excessive anxiety and dread. This phenomenon is real, affecting 18.3% of over 5,000 students surveyed, and research suggests that existing psychological characteristics, including shyness, play a significant role. As alcohol wears off, the nervous system can swing towards greater alertness and arousal, triggering anxiety. A study of 97 social drinkers found that shy drinkers experienced a spike in anxiety the following day, with highly anxious individuals reporting even higher levels. This hang-xiety can impact daily life, making it essential to understand and address this issue.

cards.title: Massive measles outbreak hits Pennsylvania, claims five lives
cards.content: In central Pennsylvania, a massive measles outbreak has caused significant pain and suffering, particularly among the Amish community. The outbreak, the worst in the US since the early 1990s, has resulted in over 1,000 cases and five deaths. The Central Pennsylvania Clinic, which serves patients with genetic disorders, is at the forefront of the response. Clinic leaders, including Dr. Katherine Mascia, are working to raise vaccination rates, provide accurate information, and build trust with the community. The clinic has hosted pop-up vaccination clinics, administered MMR vaccines, and made home visits to meet patients' needs.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Economic Damages from Carbon Emissions Reach Four Times Previous Estimates
cards.content: Economic damages from carbon emissions could reach up to four times previous estimates, with global sea level rise locked in for centuries, according to a new report. The report finds 2025 was 1.43°C warmer than the pre-industrial baseline, with human activities releasing 38.1 billion tonnes of CO2. The report highlights the need for stringent mitigation pathways to limit warming to 1.5°C, warning that beyond this threshold, risks of cascading and irreversible climate impacts increase. The report also notes that ocean heat content reached a record for the ninth consecutive year, with over 90% of the excess heat absorbed by oceans.

cards.title: New Zealand Report Warns of Rising Temperatures and Climate Change Devastation
cards.content: A new report by the Government of New Zealand highlights the devastating impact of climate change on the country. The report, Our Atmosphere and Climate 2026, reveals that human activities have increased carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, driving temperature rises across New Zealand. Temperatures have risen by 1.36 degrees Celsius since 1909, with 7 of the 10 warmest years occurring in the last decade. The report warns of increasing heatwaves, glacier melting, and sea-level rise, with projections showing warming reaching between 0.8 and 3.2 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.

cards.title: India Expects Rain, Snow, Heat, and Thunderstorms
cards.content: Northern hills are expected to experience rain and snowfall, while Delhi and nearby plains face heat and humidity, with temperatures potentially dropping by 2-4 degrees Celsius in the coming days. Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand may receive rain, with higher mountain areas potentially witnessing light snowfall. Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are forecast to receive heavy rain, with a yellow alert issued by the weather department. Several states may also face thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds, with Pilani recording the country's highest temperature at 40.1 degrees Celsius.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Japan Fair Trade Commission raids Asahi, Kirin, Suntory over beer price collusion allegations
cards.content: Japanese beer makers Asahi, Kirin, and Suntory Spirits have been raided by the Japan Fair Trade Commission over allegations they colluded to raise beer prices. The investigation centers on price hikes in April 2022 and October 2022, with all four companies citing rising raw material costs. Kirin and Suntory have confirmed their premises were searched, with Asahi also subject to investigation. The companies have pledged to cooperate fully with the JFTC. The raids follow a formal protest lodged by Japan with the US over military officials' actions.

cards.title: Weston Family Buys Boots for $8.9 Billion, Investing in Improved Experience
cards.content: Boots, the UK-based pharmacy and retail chain, has been sold to Canada's Weston family for $8.9 billion. The 177-year-old company, founded by John Boot in 1849, has expanded its business to sell health and beauty products, meal deals, and travel accessories. Despite challenges from rivals and changing shopping habits, Boots has performed well, generating £7.5 billion in sales in its most recent annual results. The Weston family plans to invest in the business, focusing on an improved shopping experience and expansion of healthcare services. The deal is set to be completed in early 2027.
